label: History
value: Abernethy sought a solution based on dark rites observed among Kanak natives in the Pacific.
unit: Obed Abernethy was a merchant captain from Innsmouth who traded extensively in the South Seas. When Innsmouth suffered severe economic decline and poor fishing yields following the War of 1812, Abernethy sought a solution based on dark rites he had observed among Kanak natives in the Pacific. He established contact with the Deep Ones, an immortal underwater race, trading sacrifices and human intermarriage in exchange for plentiful fish and unusual gold jewelry. He founded the Esoteric Order of Dagon, gradually forcing the townsfolk to adopt the cult and take blood oaths. When local opposition mounted in 1846, Abernethy and his followers quashed dissent through violent purges. Although he was eventually arrested during a brief governmental investigation, the town remained under the complete influence of his cult, and his lineage continued to lead Innsmouth into full hybridization with the aquatic beings.
note: Invented.
reader: agent:claude-opus-5-5 (R1-R3 pilot; source text read; not human; not blinded)
